description: PER-TRACER lateral inflow for the regional monotone PPM stack on a limited-area latlon patch (12x9x4, lon [0,60], lat [20,60], no poles, no zonal wrap). Two tracers ride the SAME air-mass flux through the SAME lon/lat inflow rules, each binding its OWN prescribed Dirichlet halo to the rules' qbc_{w,e,s,n} PARAMS. Tracer A's halo is 1.0 on all four walls and matches its uniform interior q==1, so every CW84 correction is a difference of equal values, each open-wall flux collapses to F = M bitwise, and devA = mqA - m stays EXACTLY 0. Tracer B is identical except its WEST halo is 2.0; the west wind blows INTO the domain, so the mismatched halo is donated and devB departs zero. MEASURED (julia, Tsit5, reltol 1e-10 / abstol 1e-12): devA Linf = 0.0 exactly at t=0.1; devB Linf = 1.8742645277859651 at t=0.1. BOTH assertions are load-bearing and they fail in opposite directions. devA==0 pins that carrying the halo as a rule param left the scheme's free-stream property bitwise intact -- it is the same invariant latlon3d_transport_cwc_regional_inflow gates, re-checked in the two-tracer setting. devB's non-zero golden is the NON-VACUITY twin: it proves B's halo is actually READ and read INDEPENDENTLY of A's. This is the regression gate for qbc being a rule PARAM rather than a free name: were the halo a free name read from the consumer's scope, one model scope would hold exactly one `qbc_w`, both tracers would necessarily resolve it, devB would sit at 0.0 alongside devA, and this case would fail -- i.e. the document is unexpressible under the old contract, which is the point. A rule that silently ignored its halo operands would likewise pass devA and fail devB. Geometry, winds, metric and the initial mass profile are taken verbatim from problems/latlon3d_transport_cwc_regional_inflow.esm, so halo independence is the only new thing under test.

scope_excluded.rust: Rust DOES NOT TERMINATE on this case: run through scripts/runners/run-rust.sh --files <manifest> --categories simulation against EarthSciAST dc76c5bf, it was still burning CPU when killed at a 90-minute budget, having produced no result. MEASURED 2026-07-28. The previous reason ('rank-3 makearray flux-form transport; not exercised by the rust binding's simulator') is WRONG as written and is replaced: the Rust binding does exercise rank-3 makearray flux-form transport -- latlon3d_transport_cwc_3d (3 s), latlon3d_transport_cwc_3d_ppm (219 s) and latlon3d_transport_cwc_moving_lid (180 s) are all armed for Rust as of this branch and pass. What is specific to the two _inflow cases is the Dirichlet inflow-halo (trailing boundary-operand) path -- the same path on which the Python binding raises an out-of-bounds index (see the python entry). Re-arm once Rust completes here in a CI-tolerable time. NOTE also that the Julia reference itself currently fails this case's inline assertion per_tracer_inflow_halos_are_independent[2] (actual 1.8742645288372637 vs expected 1.874264527785965, atol 1e-9), so the case is not green on any binding today.

blocked_upstream_bindings.python: With the esm-0.9.0 D-trailing-operand fix (EarthSciAST feat/d-trailing-operands: rewrite-target D may carry trailing boundary/halo operands), earthsci_ast now LOADS both problems -- the former arity rejection (`operator 'D' accepts at most 1 args, got 3`) is gone. The case remains julia-only for a DIFFERENT, downstream reason: the python vectorized simulator raises `index 4 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 4` during simulate on the inflow-halo (trailing boundary-operand) indexing. This is NOT the general rank-3 flux-form gap -- python runs rank-3 makearray flux-form transport (latlon3d_transport_cwc_3d / _cwc_3d_ppm / _cwc_moving_lid all pass on python); it is specific to the Dirichlet inflow-halo path and needs root-causing before python can be armed here. MEASURED 2026-07-23/24 (LSODA 1e-10/1e-12): loads OK (~104-156 s), then errors in simulate; 0 assertions run. Julia (reference) runs it. Re-classify once the OOB is fixed.
